Brief Profile of Directors

Shri Sanjay Kulshrestha, aged 57 years, assumed charge as the Chairman & Managing Director (CMD) of the Company on 16 th October 2023. With more than three decades of distinguished experience in infrastructure development and financing, he is a seasoned leader with deep expertise in urban infrastructure, project finance, institutional development and public policy implementation.

Starting his career with a Multinational Company, Shri Sanjay Kulshrestha’s professional journey spans across various prestigious roles in State PSUs, Private sector Companies and Central Public Sector Undertakings. Prior to joining HUDCO, he served for over 17 years at REC Limited, a Maharatna NBFC under the Government of India, where he held several strategic leadership positions, overseeing business operations, consultancy services and corporate social responsibility initiatives.

At HUDCO, Shri Kulshrestha is driving Company’s transformation into a comprehensive urban infrastructure financing and advisory institution, aligned with “Viksit Bharat @ 2047” vision of the Government of India. His leadership focuses on strengthening HUDCO’s role in financing sustainable urbanisation by supporting projects across housing, urban mobility, water supply, sewerage, Sanitation, social infrastructure and other critical urban development sectors. Recognised for his strategic perspective on infrastructure financing, Shri Kulshrestha is committed to positioning HUDCO as India’s premier 360-degree urban infrastructure solutions provider, delivering integrated financing, advisory and capacity-building services that support resilient cities, climate-responsive infrastructure and inclusive urban growth.

Leveraging his extensive experience in infrastructure financing, Shri Kulshrestha has consistently advocated an integrated approach to urban development by fostering close collaboration with State Governments, Urban Local Bodies, Development Authorities and public agencies. His emphasis on early-stage project conceptualisation, technical and financial appraisal, institutional capacity building and structured advisory support is poised to contribute to the development of bankable urban infrastructure projects, enabling States and implementing agencies to access long-term financing for sustainable development.

Shri Kulshrestha is also spearheading initiatives aimed at broadening HUDCO’s resource base through diversified market borrowings, optimisation of the Corporation’s cost of funds and enhanced engagement with domestic and international capital markets. His focus on prudent financial management, digital transformation, governance excellence and innovation continues to strengthen HUDCO’s institutional resilience and operational efficiency.

Shri Sanjay Kulshrestha is not holding directorship in any company other than HUDCO.

Distinguished Shareholders, It gives me immense pleasure to welcome you all to your Company's 56 th Annual General Meeting. The enduring support and trust reposed by our shareholders and stakeholders in our strategic vision and operational excellence have catalysed the Company's transformation into a diversified Infrastructure Finance Company, aligned with the grand national vision of a ‘Viksit Bharat’ by 2047 - one that improves lives, creates equitable opportunities and builds sustainable infrastructure for all. Your Company’s core commitment is ‘Financing Infrastructure for a Viksit Bharat’. Today, HUDCO is playing a vital role in national development, which is demonstrated by its status as one of India's prestigious Navratna CPSEs. As we look to scale this impact, we must acknowledge the broader global and domestic macro environment in which we operate.

Together, these forces are reshaping the way nations compete, invest and develop.

Against this backdrop, India continued to demonstrate remarkable economic resilience, remaining among the fastest- growing major economies in the world. While geopolitical developments and volatility in global commodity and energy prices exerted pressure on inflation and external balances, the Indian economy remained well supported by prudent fiscal and monetary policie s, resilient domestic demand, sustained public capital expenditure and a strong financial system. These sound macroeconomic fundamentals continued to reinforce investor confidence and support India's long-term growth trajectory. While this performance is encouraging, our greatest challenge is not simply to achieve high growth, but to sustain it over the coming decades. As India's economy expands, the drivers of future growth will need to become broader, stronger and more productive. In this evolving growth paradigm, urbanisation assumes critical importance.

02 Cities at the Heart of India’s Growth Story As India advances towards becoming a USD 30 Trillion (~₹2890 Lakh Crore) economy over the next two decades as envisaged by NITI Aayog, a fundamental question arises: where will this growth originate? The answer lies in India's cities. Well-planned cities, supported by quality urban infrastructure, will serve as the principal engines of economic growth, generating significant multiplier effects by crowding in private investment, enhancing productivity, creating employment, fostering innovation and expanding economic opportunities.

While these benefits are evident across the urban centres, the greatest opportunity now lies beyond the largest metropolitan cities like Mumbai, Bengaluru, Delhi. The next chapter of India's growth story will increasingly be driven by Tier-II and

digital infrastructure and expand ing economic opportunities. These cities are emerging as new engines of growth, offering India the opportunity to achieve more balanced, inclusive and regionally distributed development.

03 Urban Development: Improving Everyday Lives Economic growth, however, is only one measure of successful urbanisation. The true purpose of urban development is to improve the everyday lives of people by creating cities that are more liveable, resilient and inclusive. India's future will therefore be shaped not only by the way it plans, develops and prepares its cities for tomorrow, but also by how effectively those cities enha nce the quality of life of every citizen. Strong cities are those, where a young family can own an affordable home, where a commuter spend s less time in traffic because of efficient public transport, where every household has access to safe drinking water, sanitation and reliable public services, where children grow up in clean and safe neighbourhoods, where senior citizens can access quality healthcare and public spaces with dignity and where businesses thrive because of dependable infrastructure and efficient logistics.

Cities contribute nearly 60 percent of India's GDP and their role as centres of productivity, innova tion, employment and investment will only become more significant in the years ahead. At the same time, the infrastructure needed to support this transformation is immense. The World Bank estimates that India will require nearly ~₹80 Lakh Crore in urban infrastructure investment between 2021 and 2036. However, the success of this investment will not be determined by the amount spent alone, but by how effectively it transforms India's cities into productive, liveable and resilient urban centres. Meeting this unprecedented urban challenge will require a fundamental rethinking of how India's cities are planned, financed and developed.

Maintaining Best-in-Class Asset Quality: Focused recovery efforts through revised recovery policies, close Net NPAs.

Strengthening Governance and Risk Management: The Company’s governance framework is built on the pillars of financial prudence, transparency, and accountability. Over the past year, the Company has matured this architecture by further empowering its Chief Risk, Compliance, and Information Security officers. By integrating these critical functions into daily operations, HUDCO has proactively strengthened its ability to manage emerging risks and safeguard its assets. This evolution ensures that as the Company scales, its growth remains anchored in the highest standards of ethical conduct and responsible stakeholder value.

Optimising Cost of Funds through Diversified Borrowings: Adopted a diversified borrowing strategy through domestic and international sources, including ECBs, 54EC Capi tal Gain Bonds, ESG loans and HUDCO's first- ever Perpetual Bonds, supported by an updated investment strategy. This reduced borrowing costs, improved returns, strengthened capital base and enhanced ALM profile. Building on this strategy, HUDCO is exploring the mobilisation of up to ~₹9600 Crore through overseas borrowings under the recently announced Reserve Bank of India's concessional forex swap facility, enabling access to competitively priced long-term foreign capital with lower hedging costs, thereby further strengthening our resource base to finance India's expanding housing and urban infrastructure needs.

Embedding Sustainability into Business Strategy: Your Company's lending portfolio has been delivering significant enviro nmental and social outcomes since its inception by financing projects that improve the quality of life of millions and by reaching underserved sectors and geographies. Recognising that sustainability is becoming increasingly integral to infrastructure financing, HUDCO further strengthened its ESG agenda during the year. The Company deployed proceeds from its ESG loan facility towards projects generating measurable environmental and social outcomes, including sustainable water and wastewater management projects in Rajasthan and electric mobility infrastructure for the Telangana State Road Transport Corporation. These investments are improving access to safe drinking water, promoting cleaner public transport and supporting India's climate and inclusive development goals.

Building Knowledge Capital: Beyond financing, HUDCO continues to strengthen its role as a knowledge institution through its consultancy services and capacity-building verticals. Through its consultancy services, the Company supports Governments and public agencies in urban planning, architecture, engineering and project management services. Its Training arm, the HSMI conducted 55 training programmes benefiting over 3,300 officials, includin g international programmes under the Ministry of External Affairs, covering emerging areas such as public-private partnerships (PPPs), urban transport, circular economy, cyber security and energy-efficient buildings.

Creating Social Impact through CSR: Strengthened the CSR framework through policy updates, enhanced governance and improved monitoring. Some of the Company's flagship CSR initiatives, including HUDCO Pehal and Green Miles, More Smiles, were implemented through the direct implementation model, enabling greater oversight, faster executio n and more effective utilisation of resources. These initiatives reflect HUDCO's commitment to building more inclusive, sustainable and people-centric communities while reducing implementation delays and maximising the social impact of every rupee spent. Your Company's CSR initiatives strengthened healthcare infrastructure through support to AIIMS and Cancer Institutes in Chennai and Gujarat, upgraded health facilities in aspirational districts, promoted sustainable urban living through solid waste management, including electric garbage collection vehicles and sanitation equipment for Urban Local Bodies, supported renewable energy through solar installations at Government Health Sub-Centres in Telangana and contributed to wildlife habitat conservation in Madhya Pradesh.

Investing in Human Capital: Strong institutions are built by capable, committed and future-ready people. As HUDCO continues to evolve to meet the changing needs of the nation, the Company remains committed to building a high-performing and agile workforce. The Company strengthened organisational capabilities through recruitment of young professionals and experienced lateral talent, mentorship programme to handhold the new employees of the Company and pass on the corporate values to them, complemented by structured learning, leadership development, digital capability enhancement, succession planning and a culture of innovation, collaboration, integrity and excellence.

Enhancing Investor Confidence and Stakeholder Engagement: Continued to strengthen investor trust through high standards of transparency, corporate governance and proactive engagement with investors, regulators and lenders, reinforcing your Company’s reputation as a responsible financial institution committed to fostering long- term shareholder prosperity.

The strength of these strategic initiatives is reflected in the Company's robust operational and financial performance during the year.

07 Operational and Financial Performance y Record Annual Loan Sanctions of ₹1,64,758 Crore, marking a 29% growth over previous year.

y Highest-ever disbursements of ₹51,194 Crore, a remarkable 28% growth.

y All time High Loan Book of ₹1,60,724 Crore, an impressive 29% increase from ₹1,24,828 Crore in previous year. y Total Income increased to ₹13,327 Crore, which is a 29% increase over previous year.

y Historic high Net Profit of ₹4,034 Crore, registering a growth of nearly 49% over the previous year.

y Net Worth strengthened to ₹21,977 Crore, further reinforcing the Company's financial foundation for future growth. y Asset Quality remains robust with Gross NPA at 1.04% and Net NPA at an industry-leading 0.05%, supported by a strong provision coverage ratio of 94.90%.

y NPA Recovery of ₹402.96 Crore from outstanding NPAs.

y Overall Cost of Borrowings was reduced by 27 bps during the year to 7.17% from 7.44%.

y Capital Adequacy Ratio stood at a healthy 39.93%, comfortably above the regulatory requirement of 15%.

y Highest-Ever Dividend of ₹6.05 per equity share for FY2025-26, amounting to ₹121 1.15 Crore (including final dividend of ₹1.50 per equity share for FY 2025-26, subject to approval of shareholders at this Annual General Meeting).

y MoU Rating: secured the 'Excellent' MoU rating in FY2024-2 5, for the second consecutive year , reaffirming our consistent operational excellence.

y Market Capitalisation: Strong investor confidence was reflected in HUDCO's market capitalisation crossing ₹44,000 Crore.

y ESG Ratings: ‘Adequate’ and ‘Low Risk’ ESG Rating, which reflects the effectiveness of our ESG practices and our continued commitment to responsible and sustainable value creation.

y Credit Ratings: HUDCO maintained the highest domestic credit ratings of ‘AAA’ with a ‘Stable’ outlook from India Ratings, ICRA, CARE and Acuite (for perpetual debt), while its international ratings from Fitch, Moody's and Japan Credit Rating Agency remained mapped to Sovereign Rating.

08 Sectoral Drivers of HUDCO's Growth Your Company's strong financial performance is driven by a diversified and resilient lending portfolio that spans the entire urban development value chain. As a premier techno-financing institution, HUDCO is a sector-agnostic institution financing a wide spectrum of sectors - from Affordable Housing, Water Supply & Sanitation, Transport & Logistics, Renewable Energy, Social & Commercial Infrastructure, Smart Cities and emerging areas such as Climate-Resilient Infrastructure, Ports etc. These efforts are not merely about strengthening HUDCO as an organisation. They are about preparing the institution to play a larger role in supporting India's next phase of urban development.

And that larger role is...

And that larger role is...

09 Urban Transformation through Commitment to create Strong Institutions As India's urban isation gathers pace, financing alone will not be sufficient to meet the scale and complexity of the challenge. Strong urban institutions, empowered local bodies and sustainable municipal finances will be equally essential. The latest Economic Survey highlights that while cities contribute significantly to India's economic output, municipal finances remain constrained relative to the scale of responsibilities they are expected to shoulder. Bridging this gap between economic importance and institutional capacity will be critical to unlock the full potential of India's urban transformation. This places Urban Local Bodies at the centre of India's urban development journey

The importance of strengthening Urban Local Bodies has been further reinforced by the recommendations of the 16th Finance Commission. Recognising the pivotal role of cities in India's future growth, the Commission has recommended grants of over ₹3.56 Lakh Crore for Urban Local Bodies during 2026-31, including a ‘Special Infrastructure Component’ of ₹56,100 Crore for urban infrastructure and wastewater management and an ‘Urbanisation Premium’ of ₹10,000 Crore to support planned urban expansion and peri-urban transformation. The Urbanisation Premium encourages anticipatory planning -investing in infrastructure before urban growth accelerates. These recommendations reflect a clear national policy direction towards creating financially stronger, investment-ready and professionally managed city governments capable of delivering sustainable urban infrastructure and improved quality of life.

Recent work by NITI Aayog emphasizes that India's next phase of urban growth will require empowered Urban Local Bodies with stronger municipal finances, professional management, technology-enabled governance and greater access to market-based financing. As cities become more investment-ready, they will be better positioned to deliver high- quality urban infrastructure.

In this endeavour, your Company will be playing a pivotal role with its depth of experience, pan-India presence and enduring relationships that HUDCO has built over the last 56 years. Our association with States, Urban Local Bodies, Housing Boards, Development Authorities and Infrastructure Agencies spans every region of the country and provides us with a unique understanding of India's urban development landscape.

HUDCO’s ability to combine long-term finance with technical expertise, project preparation support, advisory services, capacity building and deep engagement with city governments is a rare and unparallelled combination.

Invest Window (UiWIN), under the guidance of the Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs . The name UiWIN reflects the philosophy behind the initiative - “You Win, I Win.” When Urban Local Bodies become stronger, cities attract more investment, infrastructure projects are implemented faster, businesses flourish, citizens enjoy a better quality of life, and the nation progresses. It is a partnership where every stakeholder benefits.

Working closely with State Governments and Urban Local Bodies, UiWIN will build a pipeline of bankable and investment- ready urban projects. It will help cities leverage initiatives such as the Urban Challenge Fund, promote integrated planning across City Economic Regions (CERs), and facilitate access to market-based financing through municipal bonds and the Special Infrastructure Grant recommended by the 16th Finance Commission.

UiWIN supports cities through the entire project lifecycle - from conceptualization to implementation.

UiWIN supports cities through the entire project lifecycle - from conceptualization to implementation.

10 Enabling India's Next Phase of Urban Transformation - Developing the Cities of Tomorrow India is entering a defining phase of its development journey. The coming decades will not merely witness the expansion of our cities, they will determine how future generations live, work, travel and prosper. The cities of tomorrow must be designed not merely to accommodate a growing population, but to improve the quality of life of every citizen. They should be people-centric, accessible and inclusive, where homes, workplaces, education, healthcare and public transport are well integrated . They should be walkable, transit-oriented and climate-resilient, supported by green corridors, efficient public services and circular resource systems that maximise the reuse of water, energy and waste. Above all, they should be economically vibrant, digitally enabled and institutionally strong, creating an urban ecosystem that enhances productivity, sustainability and the ease of living. HUDCO aspires to contribute to this transformation by combining technical expertise with long-term development finance, helping States and Urban Local Bodies conceive and implement integrated urban projects that deliver enduring social, economic and environmental outcomes. Through this approach, the Company seeks not merely to finance infrastructure, but to help shape cities that improve the everyday lives of people.

Meeting these aspirations will require a new paradigm of urban development - one that prioritises institutional capacity, financial sustainability and investment readiness alongside infrastructure creation.

The nation can become a ‘Viksit Bharat’ only when our cities become ‘Viksit’. For ‘Viksit Cities’, we need ‘Viksit Urban Local Bodies’ who are the implementors of projects.

Accordingly, the urban development model has to now shift from a grant-based approach to a challenge-based, reform- oriented and investment-led model , where cities are encouraged to strengthen governance, improve project preparation and attract long- term capital. This marks a fundamental shift in the way urban infrastructure will be planned, financed and delivered.

Strengthening the Urban Local Bodies does not mean that they are unable to deliver. In fact, many municipalities have already shown what is possible through governance reforms, better financial management and successful municipal and green bond issuances that have received encouraging investor response. The real opportunity now is scaling these successes across hundreds of smaller cities, which is where institutions like HUDCO can make the greatest difference by supporting project preparation, capacity building and access to long-term finance.

To realise this vision and build a strong pipeline of future business, HUDCO is deepening its engagement with State Governments, Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) and other public sector institutions through long-term strategic partnerships. These collaborations not only strengthen the Company's future business pipeline but also enable the planning, financing and implementation of transformative urban infrastructure across the country.

11 Building the Future Business Pipeline through Strategic Partnerships HUDCO continues to strengthen its position as the Government's preferred techno-financing institution by forging long- term strategic partnerships with State Governments. Over the last two years, the Company has signed six Memoranda of Understanding with the Governments of Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Bihar and Odisha. These partnerships encompass afforda ble housing, integrated urban infrastructure, metro rail, regional transport, expressways, greenfield satelli te townships and regional economic development, along with consultancy, project preparation and capacity- building support. Notably, the Odisha partnership integrates support for projects under the Urban Challenge Fund (UCF), the Bhubaneswar-Cuttack-Puri-Paradip Economic Region (BCPPER) and the Mukhyamantri Sahari Vikas Yojana (MSVY), reflecting HUDCO's evolving role in supporting transformative urban development initiatives.

The objective of these partnerships is to engage with States at the earliest stages of project development, facilitate the preparation of investment-ready projects and establish HUDCO as the preferred partner for urban infrastructure financing and development. The expected outcomes are the creation of a robust pipeline of bankable projects, accelerated infrastructure implementation, enhanced institutional capacity of State agencies and Urban Local Bodies, and the promotion of integrated, sustainable and economically vibrant urban development. These partnerships not only strengthen HUDCO's future business pipeline but also contribute to better planned, more resilient and liveable cities.

12 Future Growth Drivers in Urban Infrastructure Financing 12.1 Driving Investment in India's Urban Transformation India's rapid urbanisation is creating an unprecedented demand for integrated urban infrastructure, urban redevelopment and sustainable city developme nt. Leveraging over five decad es of techno-financing expertise, your Company is positioning itself as a strategic partner to States, Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) and urban development agencies by developing investment-ready projects, mobilising long-term capital and strengthening institutional capacity and is well positioned to play a catalytic role in financing these transformative urban initiatives.

Through UiWIN, HUDCO enables building up a pipeline of bankable urban infrastructure projects through project preparation, financial structuring and technical assistance. As these projects become investment-ready, they are well placed to access catalytic support under the Government's ₹1 Lakh Crore Urban Challenge Fund (UCF), backed by a Budget allocation of ₹10,000 Crore in FY 2026-27. While the UCF bridges critical viability gaps and crowds in investments, HUDCO finances the remaining projec t costs, provides transaction advisory and supports implementation.

Thus, UiWIN and the UCF together create a virtuous cycle- UiWIN develops projects, the UCF catalyses investments, and HUDCO delivers long-term financing, thereby generating a strong pipeline of quality assets and sustainable business opportunities for the Company.

12.2 Financing ‘a Roof over one’s Head’ – Affordable Housing, Rental Housing Affordable housing has remained the cornerstone of HUDCO's mandate since its inception and continues to represent one of the Company's most significant long-term growth opportun ities. Building on its extensive experience in housing finance and integrated urban development, HUDCO will continue to provide long-term financial assistance, consultancy, technical advisory and capacity-building support for affordable housing projects, while exploring innovative financing solutions for rental housing, integrated townships and housing-linked urban infrastructure.

As on 31st March 2026, your Company has disbursed ₹44,986 Crore under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban) [PMAY(U)-1.0] and Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Gramin) [PMAY-G], supporting the construction of approximately 16.57 Lakh dwelling units and contributing significantly to the Government's vision of 'Housing for All'. The continued implementation of Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban) 2.0, supported by an allocation of ₹21,625 Crore in the Union Budget 2026-27, is expected to sustain strong investment demand in the affordable housing sector. HUDCO will complement this national initiative through counterpart financing of the States' share, technical support and project advisory services.

12.3 Strengthening Urban Local Bodies Financially empowered Urban Local Bodies are fundamental to achieving sustainable urbanisation and improving the quality of urban services. Recognising this, HUDCO is expanding its role beyond infrastructure financing to become a comprehensive partner in strengthening municipal finance and enhancing the creditworthiness of cities. Through its Urban Invest Window (UiWIN), the Company is developing a comprehensive municipal finance ecosystem by supporting project preparatio n, financial structuring, credit enhancement, transaction advisory, municipal bond issuances and institutional capacity building. These initiatives are aimed at enabling ULBs to become investment-ready and access diverse sources of long-term capital.

The opportunity is being further strengthened by the Union Budget 2026-27 , which has allocated ₹8,000 Crore for AMRUT 2.0 to support water supply, sewerage and essential urban services. In addition, the announcement of a ₹100 Crore incentive for municipal corporations undertaking a single municipal bond issuance exceeding ₹1,000 Crore, along with the continuation of the AMRUT incentive scheme for municipal bond issuances by smaller and medium-sized cities, is expected to deepen India's municipal debt market.

12.4 Advancing Water Security and Urban Resilience Water security is emerging as one of the most critical infrastructure priorities for India's rapidly urbanising economy. Increasing urban populations, climate variability and growing pressure on water resources are driving substantial investments in sustainable urban water infrastructure, creating significant long-term financing opportunities. Recognising this evolving landsc ape, HUDCO will continue expanding its financing portfolio across urban water supply, sewerage systems, wastewater treatment, integrated water resource management, wastewater recycling and reuse, rainwater harvesting, flood mitigation infrastructure and climate-resilient urban drainage systems. The Company will also support innovative and sustainable water management solutions that enhance urban resilience and improve the quality of life in cities. The continued policy emphasis on water security through the extension of the Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 till 2028 is expected to generate significant investment opportunities in urban water infrastructure. With decades of experience in financing water supply and sanitation projects, HUDCO is well positioned to partner with States and Urban Local Bodies in developing resilient and sustainable water infrastructure.

12.5 Financing India's New Growth Engines India's economic landscape is being reshaped by the emergence of City Economic Regions (CERs), Global Capability Centres (GCCs), Industrial Corridors and Integrated Townships, creating a new generation of demand for urban infrastructure. These integrated economic ecosystems require significant investments in housing, mobility, water supply, sewerage, social infrastructure and municipal services, presenting substantial long-term financing opportunities for HUDCO.

The scale of this opportunity is significant. According to the NASSCOM -Zinnov GCC Value Orbit 2026 Report, India hosts 2,117 Global Capability Centres , employing 23.6 Lakh professionals and generating ~₹9.48 Lakh Crore in annual revenues. The continued expansion of GCCs, coupled with the development of industrial corridors and CERs, is expected to accelerate investments in integrated urban infrastructure across the country, providing a significant opportunity for HUDCO to support integrated infrastructure development through customised financing solutions and strategic partnerships, thereby contributing to India's next phase of economic transformation.

12.6 Accelerating Sustainable Mobility and Integrated Connectivity Efficient, sustainable and integrated transport systems are fundamental to India's future economic competitiveness and urban development. HUDCO has steadily expanded its infrastructure financing portfolio beyond traditional urban infrastructure to support modern mobility systems that enhance regional connectivity, improve logistics efficiency and promote sustainable urbanisation.

The scale of investment opportunities remains substantial. The National Infrastructure Pipeline (NIP) envisages infrastructure investments of over ₹143 Lakh Crore, with the transport sector accounting for the largest share of investments. Simultaneously, the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan is driving integrated, multimodal connectivity across the country through coordinated infrastructure planning.

Against this backdrop, HUDCO will continue financing Metro Rail, Regional Rapid Transit Systems (RRTS), Transit-Oriented Development (TOD), logistics parks, freight corridors, industrial corridors, ports, airports and multimodal transport infrastructure. By supporting integrated transport ecosystems, the Company aims to improve urban mobility, enhance economic productivity and strengthen India's logistics competitiveness.

12.7 Financing Climate-Resilient and Future-Ready Cities Climate resilience is rapidly emerging as one of the largest long-term infrastructure investment opportunities globally. As Indian cities face increasing risks from heat waves, urban heat islands, urban flooding, cyclones, water scarcity and other climate-related events , investments in resilient urban infrastructure are expected to increase significantly over the coming decades.

According to the World Bank, India will require investments of over ~₹230 Lakh Crore by 2050 to develop climate- resilient and low-carbon urban infrastructure. Simultaneously, India's commitment to achieving 500 GW of non-fossil fuel electricity capacity by 2030 and Net Zero emissions by 2070 is accelerating investments in sustainable infrastructure and clean energy.

Recognising this structural shift, HUDCO will continue to finance climate-resilient housing, flood mitigation systems, blue-green infrastructure, sustainable water management and heat-resilient infrastructure. The Company will continue integrating sustainability considerations into its financing strategy, while supporting the transition towards resilient, low-carbon and future-ready cities.

12.8 Advancing Circular and Sustainable Urban Development Rapid urbanisation is increasing the need for resource-efficient and environmentally sustainable infrastructure as resources are fixed and scarce and not keeping pace with the increasing urban population. The transition towards a circular economy presents significant opportunities for investment in scientific waste management, resource recovery and sustainable urban infrastructure, creating a new growth avenue for HUDCO.

According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, urban India generates approximately 1.6 Lakh tonnes of municipal solid waste every day, underscoring the urgent need for large-scale investments in integrated waste management infrastructure. HUDCO will continue supporting investments in integrated solid waste management, waste- practices based on the principles of Reduce, Reuse and Recycle (3Rs). These investments will contribute to cleaner cities, improved resource efficiency and sustainable urban development, while opening new opportunities in green infrastructure financing.

12.9 Financing India's Digital Infrastructure Ecosystem Digital infrastructure is emerging as one of India's fastest-growing infrastructure asset classes, driven by rapid adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI), cloud computing, digital public infrastructure and data-intensive technologies. As digitalisation accelerates across sectors, significant investments will be required not only in data centres but also in the supporting power, water, connectivity and urban infrastructure, creating a large and diversified financing opportunity for HUDCO.

According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, India's installed data centre capacity is approximately 1,280 MW and is expected to expand significant ly in the coming years. The Government of India has set an ambition of achieving at least 10 GW of data centre capacity by 2030, indicating that there will be significant need for investment in digital infrastructure by the end of the decade.

HUDCO will actively explore financing across the digital infrastructure value chain, including data centres, power and utility infrastructure, water systems, digital connectivity and associated urban and social infrastructure. The Company is well positioned to support the infrastructure backbone required for India's expanding digital economy. 12.10 Expanding Financing to Other Infrastructure Sectors India's infrastructure landscape continues to evolve rapidly, creating significant opportunities across commercially viable sectors supported by increasing private sector participation. As part of its long-term growth strategy, HUDCO is diversifying its infrastructure financing portfolio by strengthening its capabilities in Public-Private Partnership (PPP) financing and expanding into high-growth infrastructure segments.

The opportunity pipeline is substantial. The Department of Economic Affairs has developed a three-year PPP Project Pipeline comprising 852 projects with a combined investment potential of over ₹17 Lakh Crore, spanning transport, logistics, energy, ports, airports and social infrastructure. Complementing this, Sagarmala 2.0 aims to catalyse investments of around ₹3.6 Lakh Crore in ports, waterways and coastal infrastructure, while the Modified UDAN Scheme provide s an outlay of ₹28,840 Crore (FY 2026-27 to FY 2035-36) to develop 100 airports, 200 modern helipads in hilly, remote, island and aspirational regions and strengthen 441 regional aerodromes.

Acknowledgements

On beha lf of the Board of Directors, I extend my heartfelt gratitude to the Hon'ble Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs, the Hon'ble Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, the Secretary, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), and all esteemed officials of the MoHUA for their continuous faith, support and visionary guidance. I also thank all esteemed officials of the Ministry of Rural Development for their support.

I am immensely grateful for the unwavering support from the Ministry of Finance, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, the Department of Public Enterprises, the Reserve Bank of India, the National Housing Bank and other statutory/regulatory bodies. I convey my gratitude for the unstinting support and cooperation given by our shareholders, bondholders, banks, financial institutions, state parastatal bodies, housing boards, development authorities, municipal/local bodies and other stakeholders associated with the Company. As HUDCO embarks on this historic journey towards scaling up its targets and impact, our success will remain deeply linked with your partnership, and we look forward to your continued support, trust, and collaboration in the years ahead.

I express my sincere thanks and acknowledge the valuable suggestions and guidance extended by Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG), Statutory Auditors, Secretarial Auditors and other professionals associated with the Company. Finally, a transformation of this scale demands a workforce that brings its entire heart, soul and personal ownership to the mission. Our employees have shown an incredible willingness to step out of their comfort zones, embrace new capabilities and build an institution that is secure and future-ready. I would like to place on record my heartfelt appreciation to every member of Team HUDCO.

Together, we shall continue to strengthen institutions, finance transformative urban infrastructure, build better, inclusive, people-centric and compassionate cities, improve the quality of life of millions and partner in India's journey towards a ‘Viksit Bharat @2047’.

Thank you.
Sd/-
Sanjay Kulshrestha
Chairman & Managing Director

NOTICE

Notice is hereby given that the 56th Annual General Meeting (AGM) of Housing and Urban Development Corporation Limited (HUDCO) will be held on Monday, 24 th August, 2026 at 11:30 a.m. (IST) at HUDCO Bhawan, India Habitat Centre, Lodhi Road, New Delhi - 110003 through Video Conferencing (VC)/ Other Audio-Visual Means (OAVM) facility to transact the following businesses:

ORDINARY BUSINESS

1. T o consider and adopt Audited Financial Statements (Standalone and Consolidated) of the Company for the Financial Year ended 31 st March, 2026, the report of the Board of Directors, Independent Auditor’s Report, and comments of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India thereon and, in this regard, to consider and if thought fit, to pass, with or without modification(s), the following resolution as Ordinary Resolution:

“RESOL VED THAT the Audited Financial Statements (Standalone and Consolidated) of the Company for the Financial Year ended 31st March, 2026 and the report of the Board of Directors, Independent Auditor’s Report, and comments of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India thereon, as circulated to the Members, be and are hereby considered and adopted.”

2. T o declare final dividend for Financial Year 2025-26 @ 15% (Rs. 1.50/- per equity share) as recommended by the Board and to confirm the payment of interim dividends already declared and paid for the Financial Year 2025-26 and, in this regard, to consider and if thought fit, to pass, with or without modification(s), the following resolution as Ordinary Resolution:

“RESOL VED THAT 1st interim dividend @ Rs.1.15/- per equity share, 2nd interim dividend @ Re.1.00/- per equity share, 3rd interim dividend @ Rs.1.15/- per equity share and 4th interim dividend @ Rs.1.25/- per equity share already declared and paid for the Financial Y ear 2025-26 and the proposal for payment of final dividend @ 15%, i.e., Rs.1.50/- per equity share totaling to 60.50%, i.e., Rs.6.05/- per equity share of Rs.10/- each for the Financial Year 2025-26, as recommended by the Board of Directors, be and is hereby confirmed and approved.”

3. T o appoint a Director in place of Shri Daljeet Singh Khatri (DIN: 06630234), Director (Finance), who retires by rotation at this Annual General Meeting and is eligible and offers himself for re-appointment, on the same terms & conditions as earlier approved by the President of India, and in this regard, to consider and if thought fit, to pass, with or without modification(s), the following resolution as Ordinary Resolution:

“RESOL VED THAT pursuant to the provisions of Section 152(6) and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and Articles of Association of the Company, Shri Daljeet Singh Khatri (DIN: 06630234), Director (Finance), who retires by rotation at this meeting and being eligible, offered for re-appointment, be and is hereby re-appointed as Director of the Company on the same terms & conditions as earlier approved by the President of India.”

4. T o authorize the Board of Directors of the Company to fix the remuneration of the Statutory Auditors of the Company for the Financial Year 2026-27, and, in this regard, to consider and if thought fit, to pass, with or without modification(s), the following resolution as Ordinary Resolution:

“RESOL VED THAT pursuant to Section 142 and all other applicable provisions, if any, of the Companies Act, 2013, the Board of Directors of the Company , be and is hereby authorised to fix remuneration of Statutory Auditors of the Company, appointed by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India for the Financial Year 2026-27.”

SPECIAL BUSINESS

5. T o appoint Shri Baldeo Purushartha (DIN: 07570116), as Part-time Official (Government) Director To consider and if thought fit, to pass, with or without modification(s), the following resolution as Ordinary Resolution:

“RESOL VED THAT pursuant to Section 149, 152 and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and Rules made thereunder, read with applicable provisions of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 and any other applicable laws (including any statutory amendment(s), modification(s) or re-enactment(s ) thereof, for the time being in force) and Articles of Association of the Company , Shri Baldeo Purusha rtha (DIN: 07570 116) who was appointed as Part-time Official (Government) Director of the Company by the President of India vide order dated 26 th August, 2025 issued by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, Government of India and subsequently appointed by the Board of Directors, on recommendation of the Nomination & Remuneration Committee, as Part-time Official (Government) Director (Additional Director) (with effect from 15th September, 2025), to hold office till the date of this Annual General Meeting, in respect of whom, the Company has received a notice in writing proposing his candidature for Directorship under Section 160 of the Act, be and is hereby appointed as the Part-time Official (Government) Director of the Company, liable to retire by rotation.”

6. Raising of Funds up to a maximum of Rs. 70,000 Crore through issue of Non-Convertible Bonds/ Debentures on private placement basis To consider and if thought fit, to pass, with or without modification(s), the following resolutions as Special Resolution:

“RESOLVED THAT in accordance with the provisions of Section 42 of the Companies Act, 2013 read together with Companies (Prospectus and Allotment of Securities) Rules, 2014 and other applicable provisions, if any, of the Companies Act, 2013 (including any statutory modification(s) or re-enactment thereof, for the time being in force), enabling notification(s), if any , NHB/ RBI directions on issuance of Non-Convertible Bonds/ Debentures on Private Placement basis and any other guidelines issued by any other regulatory authority, as may be amended from time to time, consent of the Company, be and is hereby accorded to raise funds up to a maximum of Rs. 70,000 Crore (Rupees Seventy Thousand Crore only) during a period of one year from the date of passing of this Special Resolution (subject to the outstanding borrowings at any given point of time not exceeding the overall borrowing limit approved by the shareholders u/s 180(1)(c) of the Companies Act, 2013 through a Special Resolution) by way of issue of unsecured/ secured non-convertible bonds/ debentures of the Company on Private Placement basis, in domestic and/ or international markets, in one or more tranches/ combinations and including the exercise of a green-shoe option (within the overall limit of Rs. 70,000 Crore, as stated above), if any, at such terms as may be determined under the guidelines as may be applicable, and on such terms & conditions as may be finalized by the Board or any duly constituted Committee of the Board or such other authority as may be approved by the Board.

RESOLVED FUR THER THA T for the purpose of giving effect to any Private Placement of unsecured/ secured non- convertible bonds/ debentures, the Board of Directors of the Company (the “Board”) or any duly constituted Committee of the Board or such other authority as may be approved by the Board, be and is hereby authorized to do all such acts, deeds and things, as may be deemed necessary, including but not limited to determining the terms of the Issue, including the class of investors to whom the bonds /debentures are to be allotted, the number of bonds/ debentures to be allotted in each tranche, issue price, tenor, interest rate, premium/ discount to the then prevailing market price, amount of issue, discount to issue price, listing, issuing any declaration/ undertaking or any terms & conditions of issue of Bonds, etc., required to be included in the Private Placement Offer Letter/ Offer Document/ Offering Circular and any other regulatory requirement for the time being in force.

RESOL VED FURTHER THAT the consent of the Company, be and is hereby accorded under the provisions of Rule 14 of the Companies (Prospectus and Allotment of Securities) Rules, 2014, to the Board of Directors of the Company to issue any other securities (both long term and short term) from time to time up to the limits as may be approved under the annual borrowing program of the Company, subject to the outstanding borrowings at any given point of time not exceeding the overall borrowing limit approved / as may be approved by the shareholders under Section 180(1)(c) of the Companies Act, 2013 through a Special Resolution.”

NOTES

1. An Explan atory Statement pursuant to Section 102 of the Companies Act, 2013 setting out the material facts in respect of the business under item nos. 5 to 6 of the notice is annexed hereto. The relevant details, pursuant to Regulation 36(3) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 {“SEBI (LODR) Regulations”} and Secretarial Standards-2 on General Meetings issued by the Institute of Company Secretaries of India, in respect of Directors seeking appointment/re-appointment at the Annual General Meeting are also annexed.

2. The Ministry of Corporate Affairs (“MCA”) vide its General Circular No. 03/2025 dated September 22, 2025 read with circulars issued earlier on the subject (“MCA Circulars”) and applicable SEBI provisions, have permitted to conduct the Annual General Meeting (“AGM”) virtually, without physical presence of Members at a common venue and dispensation of sending of physical copies of Annual Report to shareholders. Hence, in compliance with the Companies Act, 2013, SEBI Regulations and MCA and SEBI Circulars, the AGM of the Company is being held through VC/OAVM, without the physical presence of the members at a common venue. The deemed venue of the proceedings of the 56 th AGM shall be the Registere d Office of the Company , situated at HUDCO Bhawan, India Habitat Centre, Lodhi Road, New Delhi - 110003.

3. PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF THE COMPANIES ACT, 2013 AND SECRETARIAL STANDARDS, A MEMBER ENTITLED TO ATTEND AND VOTE AT THE AGM IS ENTITLED TO APPOINT A PROXY TO ATTEND AND VOTE ON HIS/ HER BEHALF AND THE PROXY NEED NOT BE A MEMBER OF THE COMPANY. SINCE THIS AGM IS BEING HELD PURSUANT TO THE MCA CIRCULARS THROUGH VC/OAVM, THE REQUIREMENT OF PHYSICAL ATTENDANCE OF MEMBERS HAS BEEN DISPENSED WITH. ACCORDINGLY, THE FACILITY FOR APPOINTMENT OF PROXIES BY THE MEMBERS WILL NOT BE AVAILABLE FOR THIS AGM. HENCE, THE PROXY FORM, ATTENDANCE SLIP AND ROUTE MAP OF AGM ARE NOT ANNEXED TO THIS NOTICE.

4. As per the provisions of Section 112 and 113 of Companies Act, 2013, the representatives of the members such as the President of India or body corporate can attend the AGM through VC/OAVM and cast their votes through e-voting. Institutional/Corporate members of the Company intending to appoint authorised representative to attend and vote on their behalf at the AGM are requested to send a scanned certified copy (PDF/JPG format) of its Board or Governing body resolution/ authorization letter , etc., authorizing its represe ntative to attend the AGM through VC/OA VM on their behalf and to vote through remote e-voting at least 48 hours before the scheduled time of AGM. The said resolution/ authorization letter shall be sent to the scrutinizer Ms. Parul Jain, Company Secretaries approved by the Board, by e-mail from its registered e-mail address at vapassociatespcs@gmail.com.

5. In case of joint holders, the members whose name appears as the first holder in the order of names as per the Register of Members of the Company/ list of Beneficial Owners provided by National Securities Depository Limited (‘NSDL ’)/ Central Depository Services (India) Limited (‘CDSL’) (collectively referred to as ‘Depositories’) in respect of such joint holding, will be entitled to vote.

6. In complia nce with the MCA Circulars and Regulation 36(1)(a) of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, Notice of the AGM along with the Annual Report for the Financial Year 2025-26 is being sent only through electronic mode to those members whose e-mail address is registered with the Company / Registrar and Transfer Agent / Depository Participants/ Depositories.

Further , in compliance with Regulation 36(1)(b) of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, a letter providing the web-link, including the exact path, where Annual Report for the Financial Year 2025-26 is available, is being sent to those members whose e-mail address is not registered with the Company / Registrar and Transfer Agent / Depository Participants/ Depositories.

Members may note that this Notice and Annual Report for the Financial Year 2025-26 will also be available on the Company’s website at www.hudco.org.in , websites of the Stock Exchanges, i.e., BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of India Limited at www.bseindia.com and www.nseindia.com, respectively, and on the website of Company’s Registrar and Transfer Agent, Beetal Financial & Computer Services Private Limited and on the website of National Securities Depository Limited (agency appointed for providing the Remote e-voting facility and e-voting system during the AGM), i.e., www.evoting.nsdl.com The Company shall send a physical copy of the Annual Report only to those members who specifically reque st for the same at cswhudco@hudco.org mentioning their Folio No. / DP ID and Client ID or send request through post.

7. Members who would like to express their views/ask questions during the AGM, may register themselves as a speaker by sending their request from their registered email address mentioning their name, Demat Account / folio number, email id, mobile number at investors.agm@hudco.org, not later than 5:00 p.m., up to 17th August, 2026. Only those members who have registered themselves as Speaker will be allowed to express their views/ ask questions during the AGM, once the floor is open for shareholders queries. The Company reserves the right to limit the number of speakers and number of questions depending on the availability of time at the AGM.

Further, the members desirous of seeking any information / clarification on any item(s) of business to be transacted at

the meeting are requested to send their queries at investors.agm@hudco.org on or before 17th August, 2026, so that the information required/ clarification sought can be made readily available at the time of AGM.

8. The attendance of the Members attending the AGM through VC/OAVM will be counted for the purpose of ascertaining the quorum under Section 103 of Companies Act, 2013.

9. On approval/ declaration at the AGM, payment of dividend will be made subject to deduction of tax at source, to the eligible members, whose names appear as beneficial owner/member as at the end of the business hours on Monday, 17th August, 2026, being the record date.

Members may further note that, as per the provisions of the Income-tax Act, 2025 ("Act"), dividend income is taxable in the hands of the members, as per applicability of the Act. Accordingly, the Company is required to deduct Tax at Source ("TDS") / Withholding Tax ("WHT"), on the dividend paid at the applicable rates for Resident and Non-resident shareholders, as prescribed by the Act.

For the detailed process, please visit website of the Company www.hudco.org.in Investors/56AGM/TDS Communication. The shareholders are requested to submit the requisite documents, for claiming exemption at nil/ concessional rate of tax, as mentioned above and as required under the IT Act, to the Company at dividend.tax@hudco.org only, on or before, 19th August, 2026 to enable the Company to determine the appropriate TDS rates. No communication on tax determination/deduction shall be entertained after 19th August, 2026, or the documents submitted at email other than specified email address as mentioned above.

Further, pursuant to Section 124(6) of the Companies Act, 2013 and IEPF Rules, 2016, all shares in respect of which dividend has not been paid or claimed for seven consecutive years or more, shall also be transferred to IEPF Account. Shareholders may please note that if any amount/ shares are transferred to the Fund, then the same has to be claimed from the ‘Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority’ following the procedure as provided under IEPF Rules, 2016.

5. Password details for shareholders other than Individual shareholders are given below:

a) If you are already registered for e-Voting, then you can use your existing password to login and cast your vote.

b) If you are using NSDL e-Voting system for the first time, you will need to retrieve the ‘initial password’ which was communicated to you. Once you retrieve your ‘initial password’, you need to enter the ‘initial password’ and the system will force you to change your password.

c) How to retrieve your ‘initial password’?

(i) If your email ID is registered in your demat account or with the company, your ‘initial password’ is communicated to you on your email ID. Trace the email sent to you from NSDL from your mailbox. Open the email and open the attachment i.e. a .pdf file. Open the .pdf file. The password to open the .pdf file is your 8 digit client ID for NSDL account, last 8 digits of client ID for CDSL account or folio number for shares held in physical form. The .pdf file contains your ‘User ID’ and your ‘initial password’.

(ii) If your email ID is not registered, please follow steps mentioned below in “ Process for those shareholders whose email IDs are not registered”.

(ii) If your email ID is not registered, please follow steps mentioned below in “ Process for those shareholders whose email IDs are not registered”.

6. If you are unable to retrieve or have not received the “Initial password” or have forgotten your password:

a) Click on “Forgot User Details/Password?”(If you are holding shares in your demat account with NSDL or CDSL) option available on www.evoting.nsdl.com.

b) "Physical User Reset Password?” (If you are holding shares in physical mode) option available on www.evoting.nsdl.com.

c) If you are still unable to get the password by aforesaid two options, you can send a request at evoting@nsdl.com mentioning your demat account number/folio number, your PAN, your name and your registered address etc.

d) Members can also use the OTP (One Time Password) based login for casting the votes on the e-Voting system of NSDL.

7. After entering your password, tick on Agree to “Terms and Conditions” by selecting on the check box.

8. Now , you will have to click on “Login” button.

9. After you click on the “Login” button, Home page of e-V oting will open.

Step 2: Cast your vote electronically and join General Meeting on NSDL e-Voting system.

Step 2: Cast your vote electronically and join General Meeting on NSDL e-Voting system.

How to cast your vote electronically and join General Meeting on NSDL e-Voting system?

1. After successful login at Step 1, you will be able to see all the companies “EVEN” in which you are holding shares and whose voting cycle and General Meeting is in active status.

2. Select “EVEN” of company for which you wish to cast your vote during the remote e-Voting period and casting your vote during the General Meeting. For joining virtual meeting, you need to click on “VC/OAVM” link placed under “Join Meeting.” Now you are ready for e-Voting as the Voting page opens.

3. Cast your vote by selecting appropriate options i.e. assent or dissent, verify/modify the number of shares for which you wish to cast your vote and click on “Submit” and “Confirm” when prompted.

4. Upon confirmation, the message “Vote cast successfully” will be displayed.

5. You can also take the printout of the votes cast by you by clicking on the print option on the confirmation page.

6. Once you confirm your vote on the resolution, you will not be allowed to modify your vote.

General Guidelines for shareholders

1. Institutional shareholders (i.e. other than individuals, HUF, NRI etc.) are required to send scanned copy (PDF/JPG Format) of the relevant Board Resolution/ Authority letter etc. with attested specimen signature of the duly authorized signatory(ies) who are authorized to vote, to the Scrutinizer by e-mail to vapassociatespcs@gmail.com with a copy marked to evoting@nsdl.com . Institutional shareholders (i.e. other than individuals, HUF, NRI etc.) can also upload their Board Resolution / Power of Attorney / Authority Letter etc. by clicking on “Upload Board Resolution / Authority Letter” displayed under “e-Voting” tab in their login.

2. It is strongly recommended not to share your password with any other person and take utmost care to keep your password confidential. Logi n to the e-V oting website will be disabled upon five unsuccessful attempts to key in the correct password. In such an event, you will need to go through the “Forgot User Details/Password?” or “Physical User Reset Password?” option available on www.evoting.nsdl.com to reset the password.

3. In case of any queries, you may refer the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) for Shareholders and e-Voting user manual for Shareholders available at the download section of www.evoting.nsdl.com or call on.: 022 - 48867000 or send a request to Ms. Pallavi Mhatre, Deputy Vice President, NSDL at evoting@nsdl.com

Process for those shareholders whose email IDs are not registered with the depositories for procuring user id and password and registration of e mail IDs for e-voting for the resolutions set out in this notice:

1. In case shares are held in physical mode please provide Folio No., Name of shareholder, scanned copy of the share certificate (front and back), P AN (self attested scanned copy of P AN card), AADHAR (self attested scanned copy of Aadhar Card) by email to RTA, Beetal Financial and Computer Service Pvt. Ltd.

2. In case shares are held in demat mode, please provide DPID-CLID (16 digit DPID + CLID or 16 digit beneficiary ID), Name, client master or copy of Consolidated Account statement, PAN (self attested scanned copy of PAN card), AADHAR (self attested scanned copy of Aadhar Card) to their respective Depository Participant(s). If you are an Individual shareholders holding securities in demat mode, you are requested to refer to the login method explained at step 1 (A) i.e. Login method for e-Voting and joining virtual meeting for Individual shareholders holding securities in demat mode.

3. Alternatively shareholder/members may send a request to evoting@nsdl.com for procuring user id and password for e-voting by providing above mentioned documents.

4. In terms of SEBI Master circular dated 30th January , 2026 to increase the efficiency of the voting process, all the demat account holders are enabled to vote, by way of a single login credential, through their demat accounts/ websites of Depositories/ Depository Participants. Shareholders are required to update their mobile number and email ID correctly in their demat account for the convenience of participating in e-voting process.

The instructions for Members for e-Voting on the day of the AGM are as under:

1. The procedure for e-V oting on the day of the AGM is same as the instructions mentioned above for remote e-voting.

2. Only those Members/shareholders, who will be present in the AGM through VC/OAVM facility and have not casted their vote on the Resolutions through remote e-Voting and are otherwise not barred from doing so, shall be eligible to vote through e-Voting system in the AGM.

3. Members who have voted through Remote e-V oting will be eligible to attend the AGM. However, they will not be eligible to vote at the AGM.

4. The details of the person who may be contacted for any grievances connected with the facility for e-Voting on the day of the AGM shall be the same person mentioned for Remote e-voting.

C. Instructions for Members attending the AGM through VC/OAVM & e-voting during the meeting

i. The procedure for attending meeting and e-voting on the day of the AGM is same as mentioned above for remote e-voting; ii. Any person who acquires shares of the Company and become member of the Company after dispatch of the Notice and holding shares as of the cut-off date, i.e., on 17th August, 2026 may follow the process as stated above; and iii. Ms. Parul Jain, Company Secretary (Membership No. FCS 8323) failing her Mr. Vishal Gupta (Membership No. ACS 51204), Partner(s) M/s V AP & Associates, Company Secretaries in practice has been appointed as the Scrutinizer to scrutinize the remote e-voting process and e-voting during the AGM in a fair and transparent manner.

D. Declaration of Result

D. Declaration of Result

i. The Scrutinizer shall, within the stipulated period of the conclusion of the AGM as provided under the applicable laws, provide a consolidated scrutinizer ’s report of the total votes cast in favour or against, if any , to the Chairman or a person authorized by him in writing, who shall countersign the same and declare the result of the voting forthwith; ii. The results declared along with the report of the Scrutinizer shall be placed on the website of the Company , i.e., www.hudco.org.in and on the website of NSDL after the declaration of result by the Chairman or a person authorized by him in writing. The results shall also be communicated to the BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of India Limited, where the shares of the company are listed; iii. The resolu tions listed in the Notice of the 56 th AGM shall be deemed to be passed on the date of the AGM, subject to the receipt of the requisite number of votes in favour of the respective resolutions.
